Check governing headings, definitions, exceptions and current source.","text":"Claimants who have no partner (including self- funders)
78088 An additional amount for the severely disabled is applicable to a person who is permanently in a

care home if all the conditions are satisfied1.


Note: This will normally be self funding claimants, but DMs should be aware that it will also include
residents where the payment of “AA” or DLA/PiP continues for the first four weeks after admission.


                                                                   1 SPC Regs, reg 5(1)(b) & Sch I, para 1(1)(a)


Example


Shafaq has no partner and lives at home with his sisters. He is in receipt of the care component of DLA at
the middle rate and no one receives CA, or UC that includes the carer element for caring for him. The
conditions for the award of an additional amount for the disabled are not satisfied. Shafaq goes into a
care home on a permanent basis. The DM decides that Shafaq is entitled to an additional amount for the
disabled at the lower rate from the date that he moves into the care home. This is because


1. he is in receipt of the care component of DLA at the middle rate and


2. the other residents of the home do not normally reside with him and


3. no one is in receipt of CA, or UC that includes the carer element, for caring for him.


Entitlement to the additional amount continues as long as all of the above are satisfied.

temporary. In such a case the


1. couple remain members of the same household 1 and


2. absent partner is treated as still normally residing at home and


3. amount of SPC payable to them is unaffected.

Check governing headings, definitions, exceptions and current source.","text":"Temporary residence in a care home

Claimants who have no partner
78084 An additional amount for the severely disabled may not be applicable if a claimant who has no

partner does not normally live alone1. Such a claimant will not satisfy the conditions for this additional
amount while they are temporarily in a care home (see DMG 77007). This is because their stay is
temporary and they continue to normally reside at home.


                                                                                  1 SPC Regs, Sch I, para 1(1)


Example


Nasreen has no partner and lives with her son. The conditions for the award of an additional amount for
the disabled are not satisfied. Nasreen goes into a care home temporarily. An additional amount for the
severely disabled is not applicable because she continues to normally reside at home with her son.

Concept role: dwp:BenefitComponent.","text":"DMG 78270 concerns the housing-cost additional amount, not the whole Pension Credit award. It states that an additional amount for housing costs is not allowed for claimants in a care home unless their absence from the dwelling normally occupied as home is temporary. The exception does not establish payment of care-home fees. DMG 78240 allows treatment as living in the former home, with housing costs allowed, for a trial period of up to 13 weeks, subject to assessment of suitability, intention to return if unsuitable and the normally occupied part of the home not being let or sublet. This temporary-absence treatment is subject to the stated overall maximum of 52 weeks. DMG 78254–78257 set separate 52-week conditions including intention to return, no letting or subletting, a listed reason and expected duration. Permanent residence and Housing Benefit expenditure are separate exclusions. DMG 78271 defines Housing Benefit expenditure as an element for which Housing Benefit may be payable; actual payment of Housing Benefit is not stated as a condition here.
